name: agy-customizations
description: Comprehensive guide and reference for the Antigravity Customization System. Use to explain how customizations work, their loading priority, discovery mechanisms, and to guide the creation of skills, rules, plugins, hooks, and MCP servers.

name: antigravity-guide
description: Provides a comprehensive guide, quick reference, and sitemap for Google Antigravity (AGY), including the Antigravity CLI (agy), Antigravity 2.0, Antigravity IDE, Python SDK, slash commands, keybindings, and customizations (skills, rules, MCP, sidecars). Activate this skill when the user asks questions about how to use, configure, or customize Antigravity, AGY, the agy CLI, the Antigravity IDE, or Antigravity 2.0.

name: automation
description: Interactive guide to design and create a scheduled background automation. Use this skill when the user wants to create an automated or recurring scheduled task (e.g. "summarize my emails every morning", "every Monday send me a to-do list"). Also triggered by the /automation slash command.

name: conversations
description: Manage local Antigravity conversations programmatically over HTTP+JSON: create a new conversation (with an optional initial prompt), list conversations, read conversation metadata and run state, rename, archive, pin, star, tag, or group conversations, and delete conversations. Use when the user asks to list, rename, pin, star, archive, delete, or start conversations, including the current one, or when a script, plugin, or automation needs to manage conversations outside of subagent tool calls.

name: generative_ui
description: How to render rich interactive HTML widgets inline in the chat or as standalone artifacts. Use this skill when you want to show the user diagrams, data visualizations, interactive controls, educational walkthroughs, or any rich visual content beyond plain text and markdown.

name: mcp-app-development
description: Build, package, and debug MCP Apps for Antigravity: MCP server tools whose results render as interactive UI in the conversation, in the side pane, or full-page from the sidebar. Use when adding a UI to an MCP tool, building or theming the app itself, packaging it as a plugin, or debugging an app that doesn't render or behave as expected.

name: migrate-agent-settings
description: Migrates the user's MCP servers, skills, slash commands, subagents, and instruction files from other coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI) into one new Antigravity plugin. Use when the user wants to bring over, import, or migrate their setup or config from another agent or tool. Don't use for installing Marketplace plugins or authoring a new plugin from scratch (use the plugin skill).

name: migrate-workflows
description: Automatically migrate legacy workflows to modern skills across global and workspace configurations. Scans for existing workflows, creates target SKILL.md files, and safely archives old workflow files.

name: permissioned-github
description: Guidelines for interacting with GitHub and request permissions from the user when commands fail due to restrictions in the agent environment.

name: plugin
description: How to manage and create plugins — namespaced bundles of skills, agents, rules, MCP servers and hooks that install, enable and disable as a single unit. Use this skill when the user wants to enable, disable, install or uninstall a plugin, when they want to create a new plugin, or when a new customization should be packaged into a plugin rather than left loose. Also triggered by the /plugin slash command. Don't use for the underlying customization system itself — discovery roots, loading priority, or authoring a standalone skill, agent, rule, hook or MCP server outside a plugin; see the customizations guide skill for those.

name: run-workflow
description: How to write and run a dynamic workflow script with the `run_workflow` tool: a Python script that orchestrates many agents with `agent`, `parallel`, `pipeline`, and `phase`. Use when a task splits into many independent or staged pieces of agent work (fan out over files, modules, bugs, or review angles, then aggregate), or when the user asks for a workflow. Don't use for a single delegated task (use a subagent) or for legacy workflow files (see migrate-workflows).

name: swarm
description: (Preview & Quota Heavy) Run a swarm: several agents working in parallel on one task, each in its own conversation, collaborating through a shared message board. Use when the work splits into pieces that can be done at the same time, or when a second pair of eyes should check the first pair's work.

name: swarm_monitor
description: ONLY for the native-swarm worker whose brief says it is the monitor. On a timer, it checks whether the whole swarm has stalled and calls on the one member who can unstick it. Coordinators and other workers: do not load this.

name: swarm_narrator
description: ONLY for the native-swarm worker whose brief says it is the narrator. It watches the board and keeps the facts behind the user's Overview (view.json) current. Coordinators and other workers: do not load this.

name: swarm_pane
description: ONLY for the coordinator of an active /swarm session. What the coordinator writes so the Swarm UI's Overview can show the swarm's goal, its groups of work and a screenshot timeline; load it before you brief and add the first workers. Outside /swarm, do not load this.

name: ui-plugin-navigation
description: Discover UI plugin panels relevant to the current task and surface a one-click pill in chat to open (toggle) them in the side pane. Use when a running UI plugin's panel would help with what the user is doing, or right after the user enables a new UI plugin pane and a shortcut to open it is handy.

name: 21st-ai
description: Generate and iterate on UI with 21st AI from the terminal via the `21st` CLI (`@21st-dev/cli`): sketch a UI from a prompt, preview the variants in the browser, edit any variant in place with a natural-language change, and pull the final code into the project. Use whenever the user wants to BUILD / SKETCH new UI ("sketch a pricing page", "generate a hero with 21st", "make me a <X> section"), ITERATE on a generated draft ("edit the third variant", "add a toggle to that take"), or GRAB the code of a draft ("pull that variant's code", "сгенери UI на 21st", "поправь третий вариант", "забери код того наброска"). For finding/installing existing components use the `21st-cli-use` skill; to publish your own, `21st-registry`.

name: 21st-cli-use
description: Search, install and pull code from the 21st.dev catalog with the `21st` CLI (`@21st-dev/cli`): find React/shadcn components, themes and templates, print a component's code or a theme's CSS, install an item into the project, or generate a new component with 21st AI. Use whenever the user says "search/find a component/theme on 21st", "install our team's Button", "add @user/slug", "pull that component's code", "найди компонент на 21st", "поставь наш компонент", or wants to script catalog access from the shell/CI. Auto-activate when a project has a `components.json` — search 21st before hand-writing UI.

name: 21st-design-sync
description: Look at the current project's design (its shadcn / Tailwind CSS variables and color tokens) and publish it to the 21st.dev community as a shareable theme, using `21st publish-theme`. Use when the user says "publish my theme", "share our design as a 21st theme", "sync my design to 21st", "turn my globals.css into a theme", "залей наш дизайн темой", "опубликуй тему". This is the 21st equivalent of design-sync: it reads the project's design tokens and syncs them into the public theme library.

name: 21st-registry
description: Publish your own work to 21st.dev and manage it from the terminal with the `21st` CLI (`@21st-dev/cli`): publish a React component to a team library, publish a CSS theme or a template listing, edit / unpublish / delete your published items, list and reopen existing component work, and read/replace your public profile page (bento board). Triggers when the user says "publish/share/upload this to 21st", "залей в наш регистр", "опубликуй компонент/тему/темплейт", "share with team", "make this reusable", "unpublish/edit/delete my component", "change its visibility", "find/open my old component or draft", "найди/открой мой старый компонент или драфт", "add this to my 21st profile/bento", "update my profile page", "обнови мой профиль на 21st", "добавь блок в бенто", "add controls/knobs to my demo", "сделай демо с контролами". For finding and installing existing items use `21st-cli-use`; for turning a project's design tokens into a theme use `21st-design-sync`.

name: 21st-ui-build
description: Build or substantially change production UI using the current project's design context, existing components, and grounded 21st inspiration. Use when implementing a page, section, component, responsive redesign, or visual polish in an existing web project. Trigger for requests such as "build this UI", "implement this screen", "make this page production-ready", or "use 21st to create the interface". Use 21st-ui-explore first when the visual direction is intentionally undecided, and 21st-ui-review for critique-only work.

name: 21st-ui-explore
description: Explore and compare multiple meaningfully different UI directions grounded in the current project's design system and 21st inspiration. Use when the user wants options, variants, concepts, a redesign direction, visual experimentation, or is unsure how a new interface should look. Trigger for requests such as "show me three directions", "explore alternatives", "what could this page look like", or "generate variants". Do not use for a straightforward implementation with an already-selected direction.

name: 21st-ui-review
description: Review existing UI against the project's design context, accessibility expectations, responsive behavior, interaction quality, and high-confidence production rules. Use for UI audits, design QA, frontend review, accessibility review, consistency checks, or requests to find and safely fix visual defects. Trigger for requests such as "review this UI", "audit this page", "find design issues", "check responsiveness", or "fix obvious UX problems". Use 21st-ui-build when the request is primarily to create new UI.

name: 21st-video
description: Create and edit a product, launch, demo, or social video from the current project with 21st video MCP tools. Open the editable project alongside the chat, apply small revision-aware edits, check rendered frames, offer visual variants, and export the result. Use when the user asks for a video, says "make a launch video for this repo", "edit this video", or points to a selected layer in the 21st video editor. Requires the 21st MCP server.

Scans for an irreversible mutation (payment charges, deletes, sends, schema migrations), wraps the call site with governedAction(), runs it once, and prints the resulting evidenceId. Use when the user asks to "wire Strix", "wire up Strix", "add Strix to this project", "set up governed actions", "get an evidence record", or runs /strix-wire.

name: thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review
description: Run an extremely strict maintainability review for abstraction quality, giant files, and spaghetti-condition growth. Use for a thermo-nuclear code quality review, thermonuclear review, deep code quality audit, or especially harsh maintainability review.

name: ui-styling
description: Create beautiful, accessible user interfaces with shadcn/ui components (built on Radix UI + Tailwind), Tailwind CSS utility-first styling, and canvas-based visual designs. Use when building user interfaces, implementing design systems, creating responsive layouts, adding accessible components (dialogs, dropdowns, forms, tables), customizing themes and colors, implementing dark mode, generating visual designs and posters, or establishing consistent styling patterns across applications.

name: ui-ux-pro-max
description: Comprehensive design guide for web, mobile, and desktop applications. Contains 67 styles, 161 color palettes, 57 font pairings, 99 UX guidelines, and 25 chart types across 22 technology stacks.
